title: LLM context compression efficiency pilot
domain: LLM context compression and token efficiency
problem_statement: Determine whether a context-compression method reduces input-token count while preserving task performance.
objective: Compare compressed and uncompressed context conditions on the same fixed task set.
success_criteria: Median input-token count decreases relative to the uncompressed baseline.
Task accuracy remains within a predeclared tolerance of the baseline.

hypotheses.statement: The compression method reduces input-token usage.
hypotheses.prediction: The compressed condition has a lower median input-token count on the fixed task set.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Reject this hypothesis if median input-token count does not decrease.

hypotheses.statement: Compression quality depends on task type.
hypotheses.prediction: Performance differences vary between retrieval-heavy and reasoning-heavy tasks.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Reject if the predeclared task-category comparison shows no meaningful difference.

controls: Use the same task instances in both conditions.
Hold model version and generation settings constant.
Predeclare scoring rules before comparing outputs.
experiment.dataset: A documented synthetic task set for the first offline harness; later studies must document real dataset and licensing.
experiment.method: Validate the plan first. In a later experiment, run baseline and compression conditions, store raw outputs, and compute paired metrics.
reproducibility_notes: Record dataset version and task identifiers.
Record model version, tokenizer, and generation settings when applicable.
Keep raw outputs and analysis scripts with the experiment record.

risks: Compression may remove details required for a correct answer.
Synthetic tasks may not represent real workloads.
Token savings do not necessarily imply lower wall-clock latency or cost.
Results may vary by tokenizer, model, and prompt distribution.

constraints.compute: Local CPU for plan validation and tests

claims.claim: The proposed method will reduce input-token usage.
The prototype validates research-plan structure only.
